title: QuarticPairing: the pairing of the twists in Conjecture 1.2 of David, Dunn, Hamieh and Lin
abstract: Conjecture 1.2 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) asserts that the sums S_beta(X; l) of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] with N(c) <= X and c = beta (mod 4), twisted by (conj(c)/|c|)^l and weighted by the von Mangoldt function, are b_beta X^(3/4) + O(X^(1/2+eps)) with b_beta nonzero when l = 0 and O(X^(1/2+eps)) when l is nonzero. The development proves that if g(c)^2 = -kappa c/|c| for a fixed unit kappa on the support of the weight (the identity (1.2) of the same paper), then g(c) conj(c)/|c| = -kappa conj(g(c)), so S_beta(X; 1) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; 0)), and the cases l = 0 and l = 1 of the conjecture force b_beta = 0, which the conjecture excludes; the same holds when the identity fails on an exceptional set of weight O(X^(1/2+eps)). More generally S_beta(X; 1 - l) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; l)) for every l. The corrected conjecture, with main term -kappa conj(b_beta) X^(3/4) at l = 1, is shown equivalent under the identity to its cases l <= 0, and that main term is shown to be the only one compatible with the case l = 0. It also proves the pairing identities A(nu^3, -m) = -kappa conj A(nu, m) for the twisted moments and the fact behind the special role of order four: if |g| = 1 and g^k = xi then conj(g) = g^(k-1) conj(xi). The Gauss sum and the von Mangoldt function are abstract functions on the Gaussian integers, so no quartic residue symbol is defined.
